page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized, Arm-based instance type built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 9th-generation custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 48 physical CPU cores with 48 dedicated vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading, ensuring single-threaded core isolation. The system includes 96.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for compute-heavy workloads.

This instance includes direct-attached block storage consisting of 2850 GB of local NVMe SSDs. The direct-attached storage architecture provides minimal latency and high input/output capabilities for local scratch space and temporary file operations without remote network overhead. The instance networking subsystem delivers a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

From an architecture and resource efficiency standpoint, the custom Arm silicon paired with integrated NVMe SSD store yields high compute and storage density per node. The absence of simultaneous multithreading delivers predictable per-core CPU performance, though the 2.0 GB RAM per core allocation requires applications to fit within a lean memory profile. The local NVMe SSD storage is ephemeral instance storage, requiring persistent data to be synchronized externally.

The c9gd.12xlarge instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads that require fast local ephemeral SSD storage. Typical applications include high-throughput data processing pipelines, batch analytics, code compilation, continuous integration build clusters, and distributed database nodes requiring rapid local staging storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Arm-based 9th-generation AWS Graviton processor operating at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, it provides dedicated processing paired with 96.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance is equipped with 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and offers a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps on the AWS Nitro System architecture. By combining high-density custom Arm silicon with direct-attached NVMe storage, c9gd.12xlarge delivers predictable single-threaded core performance for resource-bound execution tasks. The 1:2 memory-to-core ratio and direct-attached storage make it well-suited for compute-heavy workloads needing local scratch space, such as software compilation, batch data transformation, and localized data processing engines.
